newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambican president says privatisation to continue.
newsitem.headline: Mozambican president says privatisation to continue.

text.p: Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano said on Wednesday his formerly Marxist government would continue with its programme to privatise some state assets.
Chissano said in his New Year's message that economic reforms would continue in 1997.
"Privatised companies must make a contribution to the national economy through production, through the payment of taxes, and through keeping existing jobs and generating new ones," Chissano said.
He did not detail which enterprises would be up for private investment, but the programme that began in 1989 has included banks and administration of the customs service.
Chissano's announcement flew in the face of opposition to privatisation from left-wing members of his ruling Frelimo party but the president moved to assure trade unionists.
"We will make efforts so that the companies sold off maintain their initial social purpose and that workers' jobs and rights are guaranteed," he said.
Chissano also said local council elections scheduled for this year will not be held in rural districts.
His government plans to hold polls in 33 cities and towns, but wants to exclude areas which do not administrative structures nor tax bases.
The main opposition party, Renamo, has demanded that the local elections be held in all areas of the country.
Mozambique is still recovering from a 16-year civil war between Frelimo and Renamo, which ended in 1992.
